Technique/Sub-technique: Gather Victim Identity Information: Employee Names
Reasoning: Publicly discoverable employee names and email patterns are consistent with gathering victim identity information before an intrusion.

Technique/Sub-technique: Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Roles
Reasoning: Publicly available job titles and organizational roles could provide information useful for targeting specific employees or departments.
The look-alike external domain may represent attacker-prepared infrastructure used for targeting, but the evidence does not prove who registered or controlled the domain.

A targeted external message sent to a finance employee is consistent with phishing, but the available evidence does not identify whether it used an attachment, link, service, or another phishing method.

The successful authentication by the finance user shortly after opening the suspicious message may indicate use of valid account credentials, but the evidence does not establish whether the credentials were compromised.
The finance user opened the suspicious message and then authenticated, which may indicate user interaction contributed to execution or access. The exact user action is not established.
A scripting engine launched from an Office-related process is consistent with command or script execution, but the specific interpreter and command content are intentionally omitted.
A new scheduled execution entry configured to run when the user signs in is consistent with use of a scheduled task for recurring execution.

A local security-protection setting was changed and later restored. This is consistent with possible impairment of security controls. In live ATT&CK v19.2 this behavior belongs to Defense Impairment; Defense Evasion is retained here to match the course taxonomy.

A privileged account authenticated on the affected workstation outside the administrator's normal pattern. This may indicate use of valid privileged credentials, but the source of those credentials is unknown.

The endpoint alert indicates attempted access to stored credential material. This is consistent with activity targeting credential storage, although the specific storage location and whether credentials were obtained are unknown.
The workstation queried users and accounts, consistent with discovering available identities within the environment.
Queries involving groups are consistent with attempts to understand group membership and permissions.
Queries involving nearby systems are consistent with identifying other systems that may be reachable from the workstation.
Queries involving shared folders are consistent with identifying network shares that may contain useful information or provide access to other resources.
The finance account connected to the file server using an unusual remote administration protocol. This is consistent with remote-service-based movement, but the specific protocol is not provided.
Finance and customer export files were copied from the file server, consistent with collecting information from an internal repository.
A large collection of files was copied into a temporary staging folder on the file server, consistent with centralized staging before possible transfer.
The staged files were compressed into an archive, consistent with packaging collected information before possible transfer.
Periodic encrypted web connections to a rare external domain are consistent with possible command-and-control communication, but the destination has not been confirmed as attacker-controlled.

A large encrypted outbound transfer to an unfamiliar external service is consistent with possible exfiltration. The available evidence does not establish the protocol or whether it was the same channel used for command and control.
Shared documents became inaccessible and filenames changed. This is consistent with data encryption for impact, but encryption itself has not been directly confirmed.
